units: Bekh. VIII, 1 (46ᵃ) (ref. to Ex. XIII, 2) עד שיִפְטְרוּ רחם מישראל (not שיפטרוה) provided they open the womb when the mother is an Israelite (although she conceived before her conversion); ib. 47ᵃ.—2) to send off, discharge, dismiss.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 13:5">Keth. XIII, 5</cite>, a. fr. <he>או כנוס או פְּטוֹר</he> (the betrothed has a right to say) either marry or release (me by divorce).

Gitt. VI, 5 פִּטְרוּהָ … לא אמר כלום if one says to friends, ‘release her’ … he has said nothing (they are not authorized to write a letter of divorce, as it might mean, release her of her debts &c.); ib. 65ᵇ ר׳ נתן אומר פַּטְּרוּהָ דבריו קיימין פִּיטְרוּהָ לא אמר כלום R. N. says, if he said paṭṭ’ruha (Pi.), his words stand (a divorce is meant), but if he says piṭruha (Kal) &c. Ib. ר׳ נתן דבבלאה … בין פיטרוה לפטרוה וכ׳ R. N. who is a Babylonian, draws a distinction between piṭruha and paṭṭ’ruha; our Tannai (in the Mishnah) being a Palestinian does not &c. Ib. VIII, 4. פּוֹטֵר … בגט ישן a man may divorce his wife with an old letter of divorce (having been closeted with her after he had written it); Tosef. ib. VIII (VI), 3 אינו פוטר וכ׳ he must not divorce with an old letter, in order that the letter of divorce may not date farther back than (the conception of) her child; a. fr.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 9:6">Sot. IX, 6</cite> <he>ופְטַרְנוּהוּ בלא מזון</he> and we let him (the stranger) go without provision.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 91:5">Midr. Till. to Ps. XCI</cite> <he>מי גדול הפּוֹטֵר או הנִפְטָר</he> which is the superior of the two? he who gives leave, or he who takes leave? <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 91:5">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 32:27">Gen. XXXII, 27</cite>) <he>הרי יעקב פוטר למלאך</he> behold, Jacob gives leave to the angel; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (law) to discharge, acquit; (ritual) to exempt from obligation, to declare free from punishment, eventually from sacrificial atonement, opp. חִיֵּיב.
units: <cite ref="Eruvin 65a:1">Erub. 65ᵃ</cite> <he>יכול אני לִפְטוֹר וכ׳</he> I can (by my plea) release from judgment the whole world (all Israelites) from the destruction of the Temple to the present time, for we read (<cite ref="Isaiah 51:21">Is. LI, 21</cite>), Hear now this, thou afflicted and drunken &c. (a drunken person is irresponsible); <cite ref="Isaiah 51:21">ib.</cite> <he>מאי יכולני לפטור נמי מדין תפלה</he> this ‘I can release’ means also from responsibility for neglect of prayer (the drunken not being permitted to pray).
<cite ref="Sukkah 45b">Succ. 45ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 2:5">Sabb. II, 5</cite> <he>ר׳ יוסי פוטר בכלן וכ׳</he> R. J. declares (him that did it) free from punishment or eventual sacrifice in all those cases, except &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Keritot 4:2">Ker. IV, 2</cite> <he>ר׳ יהושע פוטר</he> R. J. absolves him from bringing a sin-offering, opp. <he>מחייב חטאת</he>.
Snh. V, 5 אם מצאו לו זכות פְּטָרוּהוּ if they found evidence in his favor, they (the court) acquitted him; a. v. fr.—Trnsf. to cause exemption; to cover, include.

<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 6:5">Ber. VI, 5</cite> <he>ברך על היין … פ׳ את היין וכ׳</he> if he recited the blessing over wine before the meal, he has therewith exempted the wine offered after the meal (from an additional blessing).

<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 6:7">Ib. 7</cite> <he>מברך על העיקר ופוטר את הטפלה</he> he says the blessing over the chief dish, and with this he covers that which goes with it (v. <cite ref="I00665"><he>טְפֵלָה</he></cite>).

Yeb. I, 1 חמש … פּוֹטְרוֹת צרותיהן fifteen women (of various kinship with the yabam, by which he is prevented from marrying any of them) cover their rivals (making them free from dependence on the yabam for marriage or discharge); a. fr.—Part. pass. פָּטוּר; f. פְּטוּרָה; pl. פְּטוּרִים, פְּטוּרִין; פְּטוּרוֹת (is, are) exempt, free, opp. חַיָּיב.
<cite ref="Mishnah Peah 1:6">Peah I, 6</cite> <he>ופ׳ מן המעשרות וכ׳</he> and he need not give the tithes, until &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 8:1">B. Mets. VIII, 1</cite> <he>פ׳</he> (sub. <he>מלשלם</he>) he is free from indemnity.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 7:10">Ib. VII, 10</cite> <he>מתנה … להיות פ׳ משבועה</he> may have an agreement to be eventually exempt from making oath; <he>להיות פ׳ מלשלם</he> to be exempt from responsibility.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 1:7">Kidd. I, 7</cite> <he>כל מצות הבן על האב … ונשים פ׳</he> to all paternal duties men are bound, but women (mothers) are exempt from them.
Yeb. I, 2 כשם שבתו פ׳ כך צרתה פ׳ as well as his (the yabam’s) daughter is exempt (from the law of levirate marriage, because the yabam cannot marry her), so her rival is exempt; a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Gittin 65b:10">Gitt. 65ᵇ</cite>, v. supra.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 31b:10">Kidd. 31ᵇ</cite> <he>פַּטְּרוּנִי</he> dismiss (escort) me; a. e.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 2:1">Bekh. II, 1</cite> <he>לא נִפְטְרוּ מבכור וכ׳</he> they (the Levites) have not been exempted from consecrating the firstborn of clean animals, but only from redeeming their firstborn sons and the firstborn of asses; a. e.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 1:5">Yoma I, 5</cite> <he>נפטרו והלכו להם</he> they took leave and went.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 9:5">Sot. IX, 5</cite>.

Ber. 64ᵃ הנ׳ מחבירו וכ׳ he who leaves his friend (after escorting him a distance) must not say, ‘go in peace’, but, ‘go to peace’; הנ׳ מן המת וכ׳ he who takes leave of the dead (after burial) &c. Ib. 31ᵃ; Erub. 64ᵃ לא יִפָּטֵר אדם וכ׳ one must not leave a friend otherwise than with a word of tradition (on legal or religious subjects), by which he may remember him; a. fr.—Esp. to depart this world, to die.
<cite ref="Berakhot 17a:6">Ber. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>גדל בשם טוב ונ׳ בשם טוב מן העולם</he> who grew (lived) with a good name, and left the world with a good name.
<cite ref="Temurah 16a:26">Tem. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>בשעה שנ׳ משה רבינו לגן עדן</he> when Moses our teacher was to depart for paradise.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 96">Gen. R. s. 96</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 989:5-10">Yalk. Koh. 989</cite> <he>בשעה … מִתְפַּטְּרִים וכ׳</he> when the children are dismissed from school.

senses.gloss: to discard; ה׳ בשפה to discard with the lip, to spurn.
units: <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 37:1">Pesik. R. s. 37</cite> <he>מחרקין … ומַפְטִירִים בשפתותיהם</he> gnashed their teeth … and spurned with their lips (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 22:8">Ps. XXII, 8</cite>).
<cite ref="Tractate Derekh Eretz Rabbah 2:3">Treat. Der. Er. ch. II</cite> <he>מפְטִּירֵי שפה</he> (= <he>מפטירין בשפה</he>).

senses.gloss: to dismiss, adjourn a meeting. Y. Ber. IV, 7ᵈ top הַפְטֵר את העם dismiss the people (adjourn the meeting).
units: <cite ref="Moed Katan 5b">M. Kat. 5ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="B00767"><he>בָּכָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Chullin 51a:5">Ḥull. 51ᵃ</cite> <he>מַפְטִיר כנסיות</he> one who dismisses the assemblies, janitor, v. <cite ref="K00865"><he>כְּנֶסֶת</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 10:8">Pes. X, 8</cite>, v. <cite ref="A02709"><he>אֶפִּיקוֹמָן</he></cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: [to recite before dismissal,] to conclude the reading from the Law by reading a portion of the Prophets, to read the Hafṭarah (v. הַפְטָרָה).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 4:1">Meg. IV, 1</cite> <he>בשני … ואין מַפְטִירִין בנביא</he> on Mondays, Thursdays and Saturday afternoons three persons read from the Law …, and we do not close with a lesson from the Prophets.

<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 4:5">Ib. 5</cite> <he>המפטיר בנביא הוא וכ׳</he> he who concludes with the prophetic lesson (being the last of those called up) has the privilege of &c., v. <cite ref="Q01908"><he>פָּרַס</he></cite>; a. fr.
